text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] REDWOOD-PROD: p99 latency breach on /v1/generate (eu-west-1) — alerting oncall. Current p99 > 5s, error rate ~0.8%. Autoescalate if not acked in 2m. https://internal/alerts/1832104567

devin: taking. jumping in to triage.

devin: quick snapshot from the observability dashboard:
```
p95: 720ms
p99: 5.2s
streaming stalls: 20-45s window, repeated stalls at token ~128-256
queue depth (dedicated-pool-eu-west-1): baseline 8 -> spike 0->130 in 3m
node utilization: 96-100% (GPU mem OK, compute queued)
autoscaler: attempted scale x3, warmup per-node ~75-110s, new nodes not serving while warmup
```

taylor: noted. that warmup latency combined with a bursty traffic spike is our likely cause. looks like a mid-market customer started a batch job causing many long-stream sessions.

ops-bot: autoscaler log snippet:
```
[12:02:14] scale_request: +3
[12:02:16] provision_start node-a
[12:03:30] provision_complete node-a (still warming runtime)
[12:04:45] scale_decision: no immediate routing until kv-cache primed
```

devin: confirmed correlates with customer A job at 12:01. streaming sessions keep open long, KV cache cold so each session costs full compute. we have two pressing problems: 1) queue backlog causing tail latency, 2) streaming stalls as runtime waits for warmed layers / kv init.

taylor: two mitigations we can try now: 1) manual emergency scale (force add warm nodes and mark as warm=True to bypass runtime warmup gating), 2) traffic split to fallback model variant (quantized smaller model) for long-session routes. which do we want first?

devin: do both. manual scale first — I'll open a manual scale and bump pool by +4. Taylor, if you can prepare a route override to send long-stream sessions to the q4-small variant, that should reduce per-token compute and drop queue depth.

taylor: running override: `/infra route override --pool dedicated-eu-west-1 --match "session.type:stream && length>64" --target q4-small --pct 30 --ephemeral 20m`

ops-bot: routemap change accepted, started rolling to 30% target.

devin: manual scale command (executed):
```
/infra scale --pool dedicated-eu-west-1 --add-nodes 4 --priority emergency
```

devin: nodes are provisioning; ETA ~90s for GPU attached, ~120s to be fully warmed unless we bypass. requesting runtime team to mark as warmed when binary ready.

taylor: I applied a temporary bypass for runtime gating on those new nodes so they start serving once kernels are initialized (downgrade some safety checks). monitoring for regressions.

jordan: heads-up — if we bypass warmup gating we risk slightly higher failure rate on first-infer, but acceptable given customer impact. I support.

devin: after the route override + manual scale: p95 dropped to ~410ms, p99 down to ~1.6s for most short sessions. streaming stalls frequency reduced but some long sessions still hitting stalls at tail for specific token patterns.

kelly: which customers saw errors? I need to notify CS + send templated outreach.

devin: impacted list (observed retries/errors): Customer A (batch job), Customer C (live-chat bot), Customer F (low-volume). Customer A accounts for ~62% of the surge.

kelly: I will open support cases and start outreach to Customer A with status and ETA that we're mitigating and will follow-up with root cause + timeline. Will include provisional credit if SLA breach confirmed.

taylor: additional logs show streaming stalls correlate with a particular prompt pattern that triggers long generation loops and forces repeated KV gc events. Suggest we add a QOS guard: shed or rate-limit sessions exceeding 300s or >6 concurrent streams per tenant.

devin: agreed — create emergency rule: `shed if queue_depth > 150 OR session_tokens > 4096 for tenant != enterprise` (we'll whitelist enterprise customers).

ops-bot: policy applied: emergency-shed (queue_cutoff=150, token_cutoff=4096) — active.

devin: immediate effect: queue depth back under 60, p99 further improved to ~980ms cluster-wide. streaming stalls now mainly for the active Customer A long sessions (we're throttling new ones).

taylor: long term follow-ups we should backlog in infra: 1) predictive pre-warm before expected customer batch windows, 2) reduce warmup/initialization path to <20s for critical pools, 3) add per-tenant circuit breaker + token-aware shedding, 4) KV prefill for streaming sessions.

jordan: logging handoff: I'm taking this for overnight monitoring. Incident remains P1 while we validate customer A recovery. Devin — can you drop a short runbook summary and confirm which temporary overrides remain?

devin: runbook summary (short):
- Manual +4 nodes in dedicated-eu-west-1 (emergency bypass active)
- Route override: 30% traffic of long-stream sessions -> q4-small (ephemeral 20m)
- Emergency shedding policy active (queue>150 or tokens>4096)
- Warmup gating bypass enabled on the 4 emergency nodes
- Monitoring: p95/p99 dashboards pinned, streaming stall alert threshold lowered to 10s for next 4h

devin: temporary overrides still active. I'll leave them for 4h, then rollback gradually unless metrics stable for 60m.

kelly: outreach note posted in support ticket #INC-9854. I've messaged Customer A CSM with ETA ~45m and offered to join a bridge if they'd like.

ops-bot: created incident tracker: https://internal/incidents/INC-9854 (P1) — assigned to jordan, devin, taylor.

jordan: ok taking overnight. please escalate immediately if p99 > 2s or error rate >1% for more than 2 consecutive 5m windows.

devin: will monitor. thanks everyone.

taylor: follow-up tasks created in infra backlog: PREFILL-318 (KV prefill), WARMUP-402 (runtime warmup optimization), QOS-227 (tenant circuit-breakers).

jordan: handoff complete — leaving notes, will coordinate morning debrief. :wave:
